outcome: mode of birth (vaginal delivery or cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 309 women admitted to a public hospital in Distrito Federal in 2019 who had labor induced with misoprostol, resulting in a living newborn from a single-fetus pregnancy.
finding: After labor induction with misoprostol, multiparous women and those without gestational diseases were more prevalent in the group achieving vaginal birth, while primiparous women and/or those with gestational diseases were more prevalent among those undergoing a cesarean section.
mod_finding: Among women induced with misoprostol, 72.2% achieved vaginal delivery and 27.8% evolved to cesarean section, with parity and gestational disease being significant differentiating factors for mode of birth.
